literal: Possessors that which is called is energy; that those without, possessed thing do they possess otherwise?
translation: That which is truly called a possession is energy. Do those who lack it truly possess whatever else they might own?
modern: ஒருவருக்கு உண்மையான உடைமை என்று சொல்லப்படுவது ஊக்கமே ஆகும். அந்த ஊக்கம் இல்லாதவர்கள் வேறு எதை உடையவராக இருந்தாலும், அவர்கள் எதையும் உடையவர்கள் ஆவார்களா?
explanation: This couplet defines true wealth or possession as inner energy and motivation. The phrase 'eṉappaṭuvatu' emphasizes that energy is the only thing worthy of being called a true possession. The second line asks a rhetorical question about those who lack this energy. Even if they possess material wealth, the poet questions if they truly possess anything at all, rendering external possessions meaningless without inner drive.
